evidence: The reference behavior, as its test shows, is that a class in any extensions/generators/*.py file can be used by its class name from conanfile.txt, the -g CLI flag, and conanfile.py (reference/conans/test/integration/generators/test_custom_global_generators.py:19-81). Generated lookup needs the file named after the generator (generated/conans/client/generators/__init__.py:34), so none of those three paths works for a file such as mygen.py.

Precedence differs: the reference resolves custom generators before built-ins (reference/conans/client/generators/__init__.py:84-85, `global_generator or _get_generator_class(...)`). The generated code consults custom generators only after a built-in KeyError (generated/conans/client/generators/__init__.py:50-57), so a custom generator cannot override a built-in name.

Built-in resolution and the unknown-generator error are unchanged from base (base/conans/client/generators/__init__.py:36-37 versus generated :58-59), so the patch shows no regression for existing behavior.
criteria.deficiency: The feature's core behavioral intent is not met. Custom generators must be discoverable from arbitrary file names, as the reference tests show, and the generated code breaks that. Custom-over-built-in precedence also differs from the reference. The precedence point is secondary; the file-name requirement is the main failure.
